To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a methodology for the synthesis of DSP algorithms under both I/O constraints and memory constraints.
the GAUT tool is a generic methodology and tool for the high-level synthesis of DSP applications, based on formal models and on a generic architecture.

we have designed and implemented a methodology and a design tool for the high-level synthesis of DSP applications, based on formal models and an efficient architecture, which helps the designer to find a reasonable trade-off in terms of performance and architectural complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a generic architecture for a DSP system, and the synthesis of a DSP application on this architecture.
the following questions: (i) What is the best tradeoff between performance and cost for a given application?
a methodology and a design tool that permit the synthesis of DSP applications, taking into account both timing and memory constraints, under a high level description of the application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology and the tools we have proposed, have been proven efficient for the design of DSP applications.
the methodology and the tools developed are able to synthesize a DSP algorithm under communication constraints.
the proposed methodology and tool allow to design a DSP system under timing and memory constraints, and that they can be used in a standard Matlab/ Simulik design flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our tool GAUT is able to synthesize a FFT architecture with a performance of 2.4GOPS, with 1.4M gates and 0.8Mb of memory.
we have proposed a methodology and a CAD tool for the High-Level Synthèse of DSP applications.
we have developed an automatic design methodology that helps the designer to find an optimized solution for his application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methodology can be applied to a wide class of DSP algorithms.
it is possible to design a generic architecture that can be adapted to different applications, and can be synthesized under timing constraints.
the use of formal models allows the designer to explore a large design space in a short time.
